examples: Something about this product feels wrong
experience-architect.routeWhen: The concern is broad, undiagnosed, or spans interacting experience areas.

examples: Perform a complete product experience audit
use-all-skills.routeWhen: The user explicitly requests the full collection, or asks for substantial end-to-end product work.

examples: The page feels cramped or unbalanced
composition-repair.routeWhen: Composition, hierarchy, density, alignment, or overflow is the diagnosed concern.

examples: Users repeat information the product already knows
workflow-compression.routeWhen: A specific workflow has unnecessary steps, decisions, waits, or repeated input.

visual-identity.routeWhen: The product's identity or visual direction is weak, generic, or incoherent.

examples: Make this interaction safer and easier to operate
interaction-design.routeWhen: Control behavior, affordance, input, feedback, or interaction accessibility is the focus.

state-design.routeWhen: Loading, empty, error, offline, progress, or recovery behavior is the focus.

motion-design.routeWhen: Motion, timing, transition, or motion accessibility is the focus.

examples: Users keep getting lost across the product
product-friction.routeWhen: Systemic friction crosses screens, concepts, navigation, or journeys.

examples: Validate the screen at narrow widths and zoom
responsive-validation.routeWhen: Responsive behavior, viewport coverage, input modes, zoom, content extremes, or RTL need validation.

empty-state-design.routeWhen: A genuinely empty or not-yet-populated surface needs useful first-use behavior.

examples: Tell me whether this template look is a problem
anti-slop-ui.routeWhen: The user wants an evaluation or quality gate for generic-looking UI, without requesting end-to-end repair.

critical-review.routeWhen: The user requests a reasoned judgment on an idea, proposal, redesign, or finished interface.

examples: Trace the visual defect from the browser to its CSS source
interface-forensics.routeWhen: One rendered route or component needs exhaustive inspection, source tracing, and verified repair.

examples: Repair the AI-generated look end to end
Make this template-made app distinctive while preserving its identity
anti-ai-slop.routeWhen: An existing implementation needs source-level repair for generic or template-made design.

visual-coherence-audit.routeWhen: A rendered screen has stroke, indicator, clipping, connector, edge, or repeated-component inconsistency.

examples: Does this status pill earn its place?
The screen repeats counts and instructions
ui-necessity-audit.routeWhen: A screen may contain redundant labels, badges, panels, separators, notices, or choices.

examples: The primary game action is buried
composition-review.routeWhen: The whole-screen relationship between the primary task, supporting regions, and available space is in doubt.

examples: This error shows an internal code
microcopy-quality.routeWhen: User-facing wording may be vague, inaccurate, repetitive, unnatural, or inconsistent with product behavior.

examples: The error stays after the field is corrected
Saved appears before the request finishes
state-by-state-review.routeWhen: A built interface needs its real states, visibility timing, transitions, or recovery audited.

examples: The same tabs have different selected styles
cross-route-consistency.routeWhen: A shared pattern may drift across routes or be implemented under conflicting contracts.

examples: Tests pass but focus is clipped in the screenshot
Check desktop, phone, and Arabic captures
screenshot-acceptance.routeWhen: A release or completion claim needs rendered acceptance across required routes, states, sizes, or directions.
